target_customer: High net worth and accredited investors seeking art as an alternative asset
problem: Art is a high barrier asset class with opaque pricing. Arthena used auction records and repeat sales data to model returns and build fund structures for it.
business_model: investment fund management fees plus data and pricing technology
product_category: art investment funds and pricing data

founders.name: Madelaine D'Angelo
founders.background_notes: No background on the YC page.

founders.name: Michael D'Angelo
founders.background_notes: No background on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Statistical modeling of art repeat sales and fund structuring needed data work and securities compliance, standard for fintech.

defensibility.rationale: Auction data is largely public; the model was the only differentiator, and fund structures are copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Masterworks acquired Arthena in March 2023 to add its data science and pricing technology, per search reports.

market_need_then: Interest in alternative assets and fractional art was growing, with several companies pursuing fractional art ownership; direct evidence of customer demand was not found.

branding.domain_note: arthena.com redirects to arthena.co, which now redirects to an unrelated site; the brand domain is effectively lost.

brand_strength.rationale: Some press coverage of the product (Bloomberg, Artnet, Crowdfund Insider) but nothing about the brand itself; the name is easily confused with Athena Art Finance, a different firm.

pivots.from: Equity crowdfunding platform for buying art
pivots.to: Quantitative art investment funds and data pricing
pivots.why: Not stated; inferred from the 2015 crowdfunding description versus the YC W17 description.

outcome_analysis: Arthena started as an art crowdfunding platform, raised a seed of just over one million dollars in 2015 and joined YC in 2017 with a quantitative fund pitch. It was acquired by Masterworks in March 2023 for its pricing technology, a likely modest outcome since no price or later round is confirmed. Later round figures conflict across aggregators, so the funding picture is incomplete.
notes: Series A claims conflict: CB Insights lists 7.8M in March 2019, Bounce Watch lists 5.5M in December 2018; both single aggregators and unverified, so not recorded as rounds. Acquirer cause for failure is not public; failure tag is a guess given no price. Sources disagree on founding year (2013 YC, 2014 press). Website arthena.com redirects through arthena.co to an unrelated site, so treat as dead. No dated competitor source near 2017 opened, list empty. Do not confuse with Athena Art Finance.
